notes.title: 2026 Question Set 9: Answer in One Sentence
notes.content:
(1) Which factors lead to variety of settlements?

Ans. The factors like climate, availability of water, slope of land, fertility of land, level of development, etc. lead to variety of settlements.

(2) Which type of settlements are found in the North Indian Plains?                                                 (Nov. ’20)

Ans. Nucleated settlements are found in the North Indian Plains.

(3) Which is the most urbanised state in India?       (Nov. ’20)

Ans. Goa is the most urbanised state in India.

(4) What type of settlements are found in the central part of India?

Ans. Dispersed settlements are found in the central part of India.

(5) In which river basins in India are the nucleated settlements seen?

Ans. The nucleated settlements in India are seen in the river basins of Ganga, Narmada, Godavari, Kaveri, etc.

(6) Which rivers meet near Manaus in Brazil?

Ans. Negro river and Amazon river meet near Manaus in Brazil.

(7) Name the country which is promoting “Go West” policy. (July ’23)

Ans. The name of the country promoting “Go West” policy is Brazil.

notes.title: 2026 Question Set 14: Write Short Notes
notes.content:
(20) Importance of “Go West” policy in Brazil.

Ans. (1) In Brazil, rapid urbanisation has taken place in the south and southeastern parts especially in the state of Sao Paulo and many other major metropolitan industrial areas.

(2) The rate of urbanisation is found to be low in western and northern parts of Brazil.

(3) To avoid concentration of human settlements only in specific regions, the government of Brazil has promoted the “Go West” policy.

(4) This policy will help in reducing the pressure of population on few (southeastern) areas. This policy will also help in reducing regional imbalance in the country.

notes.title: 2026 Question Set 17: Give Geographical Reasons
notes.content:
(20) In Brazil, majority of population is found in the eastern coastal areas.                               (Nov. ’20; March ’23)

Ans. (1) The initial settlements were found in the eastern coastal areas of Brazil.

(2) The eastern coastal areas of Brazil has plenty of water, availability of natural resources, deposits of minerals and availability of transport and regular power supply.

(3) Due to these favourable factors, agriculture, trade and industries are well-developed in this region. Therefore, in Brazil, majority of population is found in the eastern coastal areas.

(21) Settlements are sparse in northeastern Brazil. (March ’19 – ’25)

Northeastern Brazil is a rain-shadow region receiving only about 600 mm of average annual rainfall, so it is drought-prone. Scanty rainfall limits agriculture and other industries; consequently settlements are sparse.

notes.title: 2026 Question Set 20: Answer in Detail / Explain
notes.content:
(33) Write a comparative note on urbanisation in Brazil and India.                                             (March ’23)

Ans. (1) In Brazil, the rate of urbanisation is comparatively higher and in India, the rate of urbanisation is comparatively lower.

(2) In 2011, the rate of urbanisation in India was only 31.2 per cent. On the other hand in 2010, the rate of urbanisation in Brazil was 84.6 per cent.

(3) In India, the rate of urbanisation increased from 18 per cent in 1961 to 31.2 per cent in 2011.

(4) In Brazil, the rate of urbanisation increased from 47.1 per cent in 1960 to 84.6 per cent in 2010.

(5) In India, the rate of urbanisation has increased continuously from 1961 to 2011.

(6) In India, the rate of urbanisation has increased with fluctuating rate from 1961 to 2011.

(7) In Brazil, the rate of urbanisation has increased from 1960 to 2010.

(8) In Brazil, though the rate of urbanisation has increased from 1960 to 2010, it has increased by diminishing rate.

(34) Write in detail about human settlements in India.

Ans. (1) There exists variety in the patterns of human settlements in India.

(2) Variety in climatic conditions, availability of water, slope of land, fertility of land, level of development, etc. variety in human settlements is seen.

(3) In the river basins of Ganga, Narmada, Godavari, etc, nucleated settlements are seen in India.

(4) On the other hand, in the hot and arid area of Thar desert, scattered human settlements are seen in India.

(5) In India, nucleated settlements are seen in North Indian Plains and eastern coastal region.

(6) Dense human settlements are also seen in plateau region of Narmada valley, paddy lands in Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Vindhyan Plateau and many other cultivable regions.

(7) Dispersed settlements are also seen in dense forest covered regions, tribal parts of Central India, western and southern Rajasthan, Himalayan slopes and land of uneven topography.

(8) In India, compared to urban settlements, rural settlements are found in greater numbers.

(35) Write a note on the urban population in India.

Ans. (1) In India, urban population is seen to be comparatively more in the states located in the central and southern part of India. Urban population is seen to comparatively low in states located in northern and northeast parts of India.

(2) The states of Uttar Pradesh, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir, Uttarakhand, Haryana and Punjab located in the northern part of India as well as the states of Meghalaya, Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland and Tripura located in the northeast part has only 0 to 40 per cent urban population.

(3) The union territories of Chandigarh and NCT of Delhi located in the northern part of India has 81 to 100 per cent of urban population.

(4) The state of Gujarat located in the central part of India has 41 to 80 per cent of urban population.

(5) The union territories of Daman and Diu, Dadra and Nagar Haveli has 41 to 80 per cent of urban population.

(6) The states of Maharashtra, Goa, Telangana, Kerala and Tamil Nadu located in the southern part of India has 41 to 80 per cent of urban population.

(7) The union territory of Lakshadweep Islands has 61 to 80 per cent of urban population. The union territory of Andaman and Nicobar Islands has 21 to 40 per cent of urban population.

(8) In India, the percentage of urban population is continuously rising.

notes.title: July 2024 Solved Paper, Assignment and July 2025 Practice Paper
notes.content:
July 2024 Board Paper — Q.5(3): Give a geographical reason why settlements are sparse in northeastern Brazil.

Ans. Northeastern Brazil lies in a rain shadow and receives only about 600 mm of average annual rainfall, making it drought-prone. Scanty rainfall limits agriculture and other industries; therefore settlements are sparse.

Q.6(A): India—Trend of Urbanisation data: 1961 18.0%; 1971 18.2%; 1981 23.3%; 1991 25.7%; 2001 27.8%; 2011 31.2%. Questions: (1) In which decade was urbanisation highest? (2) By how much did it increase from 1981 to 1991? (3) In which decade was growth lowest?

Ans. Highest in 2001–2011; increase 2.4%; lowest growth in 1961–1971.

Assignment — Q.5(3): Why is urbanisation increasing rapidly in India? Q.5(4): Why do settlements become sparse toward the Amazon River Basin? Q.7(6): Differentiate between settlements in the Ganga and Amazon River Basins.

Assignment answers are not printed in the supplied PDF; it refers to a separate Geography Digest.

quiz.question: The concentration of settlements is related to which major factor?
quiz.explanation: Availability of water is a fundamental requirement for human settlement, agriculture, and industry.

quiz.question: In the Narmada Valley, which type of settlements are found?
quiz.explanation: The fertile and cultivable land in the Narmada Valley led to the development of nucleated or clustered settlements.

quiz.question: Dispersed settlements are found in which part of India?
quiz.explanation: Dispersed settlements are often found in hilly or forested regions where the terrain makes concentrated settlements difficult.

quiz.question: Which state has the least urbanisation in Brazil?
quiz.explanation: Para, located in the Amazon region, has one of the lowest urbanization rates in Brazil.
